## TL;DR

The Work Queue now uses the same empty-column copy across themes, including the Gen Z theme. Draft uses “No drafts yet” on both the full board and its status-filtered view. The new project setting `board.emptyColumnText` provides a single override for all empty Work Queue columns. A trimmed blank value falls back to the per-column defaults, while a non-empty value replaces each default. The setting is configurable in Settings → Advanced, stored under `[board]`, and described in the user configuration docs. The tracked `repoos.toml` was not edited.

The scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed after formatting. The remote build and typecheck, changed-path tests, contrast audit, UI smoke test, local guards, and documentation link validation all passed.

## Work and rationale

I followed the existing board settings flow used by `board.doneCollapsedByDefault`: config defaults and types live in core, the schema registers user-facing settings, the config store exposes persisted values to the UI, and Settings uses schema metadata to render and save controls. This keeps the setting in the standard config path, so updates are delivered through the normal live config update behavior without requiring a server restart.

In `BoardColumn.vue`, I replaced the two theme-specific empty-copy maps with one per-status default map. The displayed copy is selected from a trimmed, non-empty `board.emptyColumnText` value when present; otherwise the column’s default is used. The existing Gen Z styling remains in the board-column rendering path, so its small gradient square and other empty-state styling are unaffected. Collapsed columns and the Inputs page do not use this empty text path and were left alone.

`WorkView.vue` previously passed a literal dash for Draft in the full board and the single-status view. Removing those props lets both paths use the same Draft default as the rest of the board. This also avoids maintaining duplicate wording in the view and the column component.

The setting is registered as a live string in the config schema, added to the supported TOML key list and the typed board config, and surfaced as “Empty column text” in the existing Advanced settings tab. The control uses the normal setting row and save path; it does not add a new settings surface. `user-docs/configuration.md` now documents the key and the Settings location.

Coverage was added at the core and UI levels. Core tests verify the empty default, an explicit override, whitespace input, and both schema and supported-key registration. The board-column test mounts each status under both classic and Gen Z themes and checks default copy, override copy, and whitespace fallback. Settings tests verify the Advanced control and that editing it saves the `board.emptyColumnText` value. Existing column-label tests also assert Draft no longer receives dash text in either board route.

## Approaches tried

I first kept the selected empty text inside `BoardColumn.vue`, based on the column status and the config store. That keeps the display rule beside the empty-state presentation while allowing WorkView to remain concerned with board composition. I also initially asserted the Settings row’s parent relationship by querying the mounted wrapper’s root DOM. That was unreliable for this view’s fragment structure and multiple mounted Settings wrappers. I changed the assertion to query the row through the Advanced panel selector, which tests the actual user-visible tab relationship and passed in isolation.

The first full check caught formatting drift in that test edit after the remote build and test work had completed. I ran the prescribed formatter and reran the entire scoped check against the resulting checkpoint instead of relying on the earlier remote success.

## Challenges and blockers

The remote changed-path run is extensive: it selected 617 changed and always-run test files, and required about 20 minutes per attempt in this environment. The first attempt exposed the Settings test assertion issue; after correcting that test, the next attempt exposed only formatting. The formatted rerun completed successfully. The repeated test output includes expected warnings from unrelated legacy tests, but the final test, contrast, smoke, and guard results were green.

No product or implementation blocker remains. No live server or browser session was started; the task’s required automated UI smoke test passed, and the declared Work Queue screenshot capture is available to the managed handoff process.

## Key learnings

The config schema is part of the supported user-facing configuration contract: adding a project setting requires keeping its type, default, schema entry, supported-key registration, Settings control, docs, and tests aligned. Reading the schema-driven Settings implementation before adding the control made it possible to reuse the established save behavior and tab placement.

A board’s empty text is presentation data shared by every theme, while theme-specific visual treatment can remain separate. Keeping wording in one status map and trimming the override at display time makes whitespace behave like an unset value without changing the persisted text or requiring destructive normalization. Removing the two Draft dash props ensures full-board and filtered rendering follow the same default path.

Finally, the scoped check can do substantial remote work before a local guard reports failure. The final result must be taken from the completed command, including its local steps, not inferred from the successful remote build and test phase alone.
